injectDaemonIdentity.defect: #84, found while validating 0.6.2: the injection fast path could be served by a daemon that was not the installed plugin, so a hook could receive context computed by a different build.
injectDaemonIdentity.design: A handshake now settles identity before any computation: the hook and the daemon must agree on five fields, and a SHA-256 of the bundle binds the answer to the build that produced it. The design was reviewed by Codex before implementation, and an implementation review folded six further defects into the same PR.
injectDaemonIdentity.reviewProvenance: Both the design review and the implementation review were Codex passes arranged by this project; they are not an outside audit.
injectDaemonIdentity.behaviour: A mismatching, older or timing-out daemon falls back in-process and records daemon.reason and daemon.got rather than serving a foreign answer. Socket ownership uses an O_EXCL lock, reclaims dead sockets and non-socket files left by SIGKILL, does not intervene on EACCES, and supports retire handover with refusal from a non-installed root. Only a listener at the installed root is accepted, MEMEX_INJECT_DAEMON can force the path, and doctor reports inject-daemon judged against the installed root without its probe contaminating inject-output.
injectDaemonIdentity.regressions: test/inject-daemon-slice.test.mjs, 17 cases: rejection of a daemon with no handshake or any single differing field with via "fallback" plus daemon.reason, the fast path served and attributed on a match, a real daemon against a real hook so that a disagreement between the two files' identity computations surfaces as fallback, reclaim of sockets and non-socket files left by SIGKILL, EACCES non-intervention, live and stale bind locks, retire handover and non-installed-root refusal, the installed-root policy with MEMEX_INJECT_DAEMON, and doctor's three verdicts. One case asserts the mismatching daemon was never asked to compute at all.
injectDaemonIdentity.knownCost: The per-call SHA-256 of the bundle is documented at roughly 5-10 ms on the fast path and is not measured by any gate; see webUi.benchmark.knownUnmeasuredCost.
injectDaemonIdentity.liveDaemonTakeover: NOT_PROVEN: socket handover, reclaim and the installed-root policy were exercised in isolated fixtures. No live daemon on the user's own root was taken over or retired, which is verified after release.

reviewRemediation.source: The external code review of v0.5.2..v0.6.1 by Codex gpt-6-astra at low reasoning effort, which raised 22 findings numbered #59 to #80.
reviewRemediation.status: All 22 findings are now closed across two releases.

closedInThisRelease.verifiedFromChangelog: The 0.6.3 changelog body cites every one of these nine numbers; #79 and #80 appear together as (#79, #80). Its header writes the range (#59-#80), which is the review's extent.

reviewRemediation.arithmetic: 13 closed in 0.6.2 plus 9 closed here accounts for all 22.
reviewRemediation.regressions: The nine land across test/ontology-classifier.test.ts and test/ontology-taxonomy-repair.test.ts for the taxonomy epoch work (#73), test/capsule-size-truncation.test.ts for list-item caps (#85) and for the control-character scalar budget (#74), test/continuity-identity.test.ts, test/fact-tier-ladder.test.ts, test/injection-gate-observability.test.ts, test/recall-receipt-observability.test.ts, test/plugin-root-slice.test.mjs, test/lifecycle-slice.test.mjs, and the UI suites ui/test/core.cjs for audit-path pinning (#78) and ui/test/guidance.test.cjs for the model-call-failed versus model-invalid-json class (#79, #80).
reviewRemediation.reviewClosure: NOT_PROVEN: that these fixes resolve what the reviewer described is this project's own verification. The reviewer did not re-run the review against 0.6.3, so "all 22 closed" means all 22 were addressed with reproducing regressions, not that an outside party agreed they are closed.

crossDeviceSync.switchDefault: Cross-device sync still ships OFF, with MEMEX_SYNC_DIR taking precedence over the configured shared folder, and the UI opening with export and import disabled.

crossDeviceSync.completedInThisRelease: 0.6.3 completes the file-transfer surface (#48): manual generation files as zip containers, device aliases, and SYNC_IMPORTED conflict history.
crossDeviceSync.regressions: test/zip.test.ts, 5 cases: store and deflate round trips with deterministic bytes, interoperability with the system zip and unzip, zip-slip name rejection, and failure rather than partial results on a truncated container, a CRC mismatch or an entry/size cap, plus the standard CRC-32 value. test/sync-control.test.ts adds the manual generation-file path with sync off — export to zip, preview reporting no change, import, and re-import idempotency — and refusal of a file from this same device, a non-zip, a non-generation and a corrupted payload, with the export path unable to escape the data root; device aliases stored locally with only this device's name propagated in the manifest and the local name beating a peer's; and SYNC_IMPORTED conflict history recorded in both directions, not duplicated on re-importing the same generation, and never carried in the export payload. The browser probes syncArchive and importedFact cover the same round trip through the UI.
crossDeviceSync.liveTwoDeviceRoundTrip: NOT_PROVEN: every sync case ran in isolated fixtures on one host, which proves the container, alias and conflict-history contracts, not a real two-device exchange. The user will test this on two Macs.

testIsolationIncident.whenFound: During 0.6.3 development, by the isolation check introduced in 0.6.1.
testIsolationIncident.leak: The `taxonomy epoch vs privacy purge (P1/P2 v4)` block in test/ontology-classifier.test.ts set only TEST_DB_PATH. The #73 regressions call mergeCategories and renameCategory, which each append a metadata line to <getMemexHome()>/logs/ui-audit.jsonl, so getMemexHome() fell through to the user's real root and eight ontology-merge / ontology-rename rows landed in ~/.config/memex/logs/ui-audit.jsonl.
testIsolationIncident.scope: That one block was the only leak; test/ontology-taxonomy-repair.test.ts and test/ontology-cli-slice.test.mjs already pinned MEMEX_HOME.
testIsolationIncident.fix: The block now pins MEMEX_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to its temp directory and restores both afterwards. MEMEX_HOME alone decides getMemexHome(); XDG_CONFIG_HOME is pinned as well so the fallback cannot reach a real directory if that precedence ever changes. Both tests now also assert the audit line is readable under the temp home, so isolation is proven by the suite itself rather than only by the external check.
testIsolationIncident.thisGateResult: PASS: 110 files compared before and after the full run, 0 added, 0 removed, 0 modified.
testIsolationIncident.significance: This is the second leak of exactly this shape the check has caught; the first, in 0.5.0 QA, put 21 lines into the same file from test/web-ui-db-factory.test.mjs. The pattern is a suite isolating only a database path while a code path resolves the home directory independently.
testIsolationIncident.caveat: The eight leaked rows were written to the user's real audit log during development and are not removed by this fix; the check proves the gate run is clean now, not that the earlier write was undone.

realRootIsolation.mode: read-only; snapshot before the gates, compare after, as docs/VERIFICATION.md §4 now requires
realRootIsolation.volatileExclusions: run-locks/ and unix sockets are excluded by default because they exist only while something is running; --strict was not used.
realRootIsolation.motivation: 0.5.0 QA found test/web-ui-db-factory.test.mjs isolating only MEMEX_DB_PATH and appending 21 lines to the real logs/ui-audit.jsonl. That suite is now inside the widened mjs gate, and this run leaves the real root byte-identical.
realRootIsolation.caveat: This proves the gate run did not write to the root, not that the root is healthy. Judgement is by content hash, so a read-only access that only moves atime is correctly not a failure.

releaseConclusion: Every gate in the list docs/VERIFICATION.md §2 documents at this SHA passes on the clean v0.6.3 candidate a1d8c486, each on its first attempt: the real-root snapshot, typecheck, a build that reproduced the tracked dist/, 118 files / 1189 Vitest tests, 182 tests through the widened mjs glob, installer, marketplace, packaged runtime (memex-0.6.3.tgz, 329 files, 9 MCP tools), offline lifecycle 9/9 with 13 owned hook entries, 148 Workspace unit tests, 21 real-Chrome Workspace probes with 0 runtime errors including the new syncArchive round trip and importedFact, isolated plugin validation, the benchmark contract, the pack dry-run and the closing real-root comparison. That comparison is the headline evidence of this release: 110 files compared before and after, 0 added, 0 removed, 0 modified. It matters because during 0.6.3 development the check caught the taxonomy-epoch block in test/ontology-classifier.test.ts pinning only TEST_DB_PATH and writing eight ontology-merge and ontology-rename rows into the user's real ~/.config/memex/logs/ui-audit.jsonl; that block now pins MEMEX_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME and asserts the audit line under its temp home, so the suite proves its own isolation. This is the second leak of that shape the check has caught, and the eight rows already written were not removed by the fix. The release also closes the last nine findings of the external review of 0.6.0-0.6.1, bringing all 22 to closed across two releases, completes the cross-device sync file-transfer surface with zip generation files, device aliases and SYNC_IMPORTED history, and fixes the inject-daemon ownership defect #84 with a five-field handshake and a bundle SHA-256 so a foreign build can never serve the fast path. The benchmark was not re-run for a third release and is carried forward from the v0.6.0 candidate: benchmarkOnThisSha is NOT_PROVEN, and the #84 handshake's documented ~5-10 ms per hook call sits on the AC_PERF_03 path that the carried-forward number predates, so that cost is unmeasured rather than shown to be acceptable. A live two-device sync round trip, which the user will run on two Macs, a live daemon takeover on the user's own root, the reviewer's own re-confirmation that the 22 findings are closed, a fresh live injection-yield check for this release, live tier placement and migration, an authenticated Codex tier run, the formal plugin validator, real-world performance at production corpus sizes and model quality all remain NOT_PROVEN.
